why:
The baseline came in at 2.02383, and the variant I tried only gained about 3%, which is within noise. I have 250 energy left and can either try another faster approach or stop here. Since speed is the fitness, I'm weighing a bigger change like the csv module or regex, but splitting bytes is likely already the fastest pure-Python option, and numpy may not be available. The gains look small compared to what the energy would cost.

I'm considering one more variant that avoids splitting per line. The idea is to replace newlines with commas and split the whole buffer once, so the category and value tokens fall into fixed positions after the header.

I'm settling on the trailing-token case: the zip will truncate to the shorter list, and the leftover empty entry lands in an id position, so the cat and val columns still line up. Then I'll sum the values in a loop and convert each one to a float. The plan is to test this as a single variant at low cost.
